title: Production of Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma for Boosting In Vitro Human Fibroblast Expansion
protocol: Open the tube blister pack for PRP preparation.
Perform venous puncture and fill the desired number of PRP tubes with whole blood.
Carefully turn the tubes upside down several times to mix the blood with anticoagulant.
Remove 100 μL of total whole blood using a 1 mL syringe for further blood cell number counts.
Ensure that the centrifuge is correctly balanced before starting it.
Prepare a counterbalance tube with water to the same level as the blood in the PRP tube if necessary.
Place the filled tubes in the centrifuge opposite each other, ensuring balance.
Centrifuge samples at 1,500 x g for 5 min.
Gently invert the PRP tube 20 times to resuspend the platelet deposit in the plasma supernatant.
Take the plasma solution from the tube using a syringe transfer device connected to a 10 mL syringe.
Keep the PRP solution at room temperature under the safety cabinet until future use.
Determine platelet concentration, mean platelet volume, and number of red and white blood cells using an automated hematology analyzer.
Withdraw 100 µL of PRP solution carefully.
Transfer withdrawn PRP to a 1.5 mL tube.
Wash skin samples in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) by gently shaking in a 50 mL polypropylene tube.
Remove subcutaneous fat tissue using forceps and scissors if the sample is larger than 10 cm².
Cut tissue into approximately 0.5 cm x 1.5 cm strips using a sterile scalpel after fat trimming.
Add 5 mL of collagenase-dispase mix to a sterile 15 mL tube.
Transfer cut tissue pieces to the collagenase-dispase mix solution, ensuring complete submersion.
Place the tubes in an incubator at 37 °C with orbital shaking for 150 min.
After incubation, place the tube containing the tissue in the biosafety cabinet.
Place the lid of a sterile 100 mm culture dish upside down in the biosafety cabinet.
Transfer the digested tissue solution to the bottom of the 100 mm culture dish without splashing.
If any pieces of tissue remain in the tube, use a sterile 1 mL pipette or sterile forceps to transfer the tissue pieces to the bottom of the 100 mm culture dish.
With the epidermis strip facing up, separate the intact epidermis sheet from the dermis using two pairs of forceps.
Hold the dermis of the tissue strip with a pair of forceps and the edge of the epidermis with another pair of forceps.
Peel the dermis and epidermis apart in two pieces, keeping the separated pieces on the same lid.
Transfer the dermal pieces to a new 100 mm culture dish containing PBS.
Using laboratory forceps, place the dermal pieces in a 15 mL polypropylene tube with 3 mL of 0.3% trypsin/PBS.
Incubate for 10-20 min in a 37 °C water bath and invert the tube several times every 2−3 min.
To stop the enzymatic reaction, add 3−5 mL of ice-cold complete growth medium (Dulbecco’s modified Eagle medium [DMEM] or RPMI containing 10% FBS).
Vortex the tube vigorously several times.
Filter the fibroblast suspension through an 85 μm nylon mesh to remove dermal debris.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 150 x g, at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 100−1,000 μL of complete growth medium.
Count the number of total and viable cells using trypan blue mixed with the cell suspension.

Plate 3−10 x 10^4 cells in 5 mL of complete FBS growth medium (DMEM, 10% FBS heat-inactivated for 60 min at 56 °C, 1% 1 M HEPES buffer solution, 1% 100x nonessential amino acid mixture, 1% 100x L-glutamine, 1% 100x penicillin/streptomycin, 1% 100x sodium pyruvate) in a 25 cm² tissue culture flask.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C.
On day 2, aspirate the medium containing nonadherent cells and add fresh medium.
Change the medium every 3−4 days until the culture reaches 70−80% confluency.
Wash fibroblasts with PBS.
Incubate fibroblasts with trypsin/EDTA solution for 3 min at 37 °C in the incubator.
Add 3−5 mL of warm complete growth medium to stop the reaction.
Take an aliquot of the cell suspension to count cells using a haemocytometer.
Centrifuge the suspension for 5 min at 200 x g.
Remove the medium by aspiration.

Culture fibroblasts in PRP medium (DMEM, 20% PRP, 1% HEPES buffer, 1% nonessential amino acid mixture, 1% L-glutamine, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 1% sodium pyruvate, 2 U/mL heparin) in the incubator at 37 °C.

Seed fibroblasts (passage 2) in 24 well plates at a density of 8 x 10^3 cells per well in PRP medium with different PRP concentrations and 2 U/mL heparin or under classical culture conditions (10% FBS).
Culture the seeded fibroblasts for 7 days.
Add a vital dye (cell proliferation violet) to the cells after 7 days of culture.
Assess fibroblast proliferation by flow cytometry.
Seed cells in 96 well black/clear flat bottom plates at a concentration of 1 x 10^5 cells/mL in complete FBS growth DMEM supplemented with 0.5% FBS for 24 h.
Treat cells with 10% FBS or different PRP concentrations (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50%) for 7 days.
Fix the fibroblasts with 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min.
Permeabilize the fibroblasts with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 min at room temperature.
Stain the fibroblasts with 50 μL of 5 U/mL phalloidin.
Wash the fibroblasts twice with PBS.
Mark the fibroblasts with 50 μL of 1 mg/mL 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) for 5 min.
